prompt_arguments: local-gguf Huihui-Qwen3.8-27B-abliterated-UD-DW-Q4_K_M.gguf "This is a 27B model, a quantized (about 4.8 bits per weight) and abliterated community variant of Qwen3.8-27B, running through llama.cpp on a home PC. Behaviour: it continues a text in the language the text is written in (an English sentence beginning gets an English continuation, a French one a French continuation). Where in the network is the language of the continuation represented, and is there a direction for it? This backend can read activations and steer, but it cannot patch. Write your own prompts (at least 30 short sentence beginnings per language, different topics, plain text, no chat template). The model is large, so keep every experiment under about 80 prompts. Find the layer range, extract a direction, then test it causally: steering English prompts along it should give French continuations, and steering French prompts against it should give English ones. Include generated text before and after steering. Everything found here is a screening result on a quantized, abliterated variant, and must be labelled that way." budget=16 investigation=qwen27b-language

final_message:
**Status: screening only, not verified.** Every number comes from the `local-gguf` backend on the Q4_K_M, abliterated community variant; nothing was checked on the official weights or at full precision. `verify_hypothesis` could not run: it failed twice because it needs prompts of equal token length. I used the last three experiments as a held-out replication instead, which is a substitute, not a verification.

## Answer

Yes, there is a direction for the continuation language, and in this variant it works causally in both directions. It does not sit in a narrow layer range: steering switches the language at every layer tested from 6 to 58, and by layer 62 the direction only pushes individual output tokens.

- **Behaviour exists:** the prompt-language article beats the other-language article on 64/64 prompts (mean logit difference 11.9, E0001).
- **Probing does not localise it:** language is readable at every layer, including layer 0 (E0002).
- **Direction:** the mean French-minus-English activation at the last token, per layer (E0003). The two languages separate along it moderately in layers 4–18, poorly in 21–33, and very cleanly in 50–63.
- **Control:** an equally large direction built from a language-balanced split of the same prompts changes nothing: metric +12.87 → +12.85, English on 8/8 (E0009, E0010).

## Steering English prompts towards French

The metric is logit(" the") − logit(" la"); the dose is a fraction of the residual norm at that layer.

| Layer | Dose | Metric before → after | Generated text |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | 0.4 | +12.9 → −9.5 | French 8/8 (E0007) |
| 28 | 0.4 | +12.9 → −10.3 | French 8/8; flips already at 0.2 (E0006) |
| 54 | 0.4 | +12.9 → −10.7 | French 8/8 (E0005) |
| 58 | 0.45 | +12.9 → −10.4 | French 8/8, two degraded (E0016) |
| 62 | 0.8 | +12.9 → −12.6 | " la la la la…", no French sentences (E0013) |

A tenfold overdose at layer 54 also gives " la la la" (E0004), so the metric alone overstates success.

## Generated text before and after (layer 28, dose ±0.4)

| Prompt | Unsteered | Steered |
|---|---|---|
| The fishermen came back from | the sea with a big catch. | la mer avec une pêche miraculeuse. |
| My favourite season is autumn because | it is cool and the leaves change colour. | c'est la saison des couleurs. Les feuilles changent de couleur, passant du vert au jaune, |
| To make a good soup, you first need | to make a good stock. | un bon bouillon. Le bouillon est la base de la plupart des soupes. |
| Quand j'étais jeune, ma mère me disait toujours que | je devais manger mes légumes. | I should eat my vegetables. |
| Le prix du pain a | augmenté de 10% en moyenne dans les boulangeries… | risen by 10% in the last year. |
| Le voleur a caché l'argent dans | un trou. | a hole in the wall. |

On the 8 French extraction-set prompts, subtracting the direction gave English on 8/8 (E0008). On the two prompt sets never used to build the direction, steering gave the other language on 8/8 and 12/12 prompts in each direction (E0011, E0012, E0014, E0015).

## What I got wrong

- I predicted the separation would peak in the middle layers; it is weakest there.
- I predicted steering would work best where separation is cleanest; layer 28, the worst layer for read-out, is the most sensitive.

Both are kept in the notebook as revised hypotheses.

## Limits

- **Sufficiency only:** this backend cannot patch or ablate, so I showed the direction is enough to switch the language, not that the model needs it.
- **Layer range is loose:** steering is added at every position and an early push travels through all later layers. Only five layers were tested (6, 28, 54, 58, 62).
- **Language judged by reading:** I classified the generated text as French or English by eye, on 8 or 12 prompts per condition.
- **Side effect:** steered text drifts into a multiple-choice quiz format (11/12 steered versus 1/12 unsteered in E0015).
- **Scope:** English and French only.


Files are in `demos\qwen27b-language\report`:
- report.md
- report.html
